title: One image, three registries
summary: A two-stage build produces one distroless runtime image. It is scanned, tagged with a version and a commit SHA, and pushed unchanged to Docker Hub, Azure Container Registry and Amazon ECR, where the manifest digest is identical.

components.name: Operator workstation
components.note: Version and commit SHA are read from package.json and git, never typed by hand, and written into OCI labels. Pushes are manual; a tag-triggered workflow is the next step.

components.name: Build stage
components.note: Manifests are copied before source so a code change does not re-run npm ci. The server is bundled into one file, so the runtime needs no node_modules.

components.name: Runtime image 1.1.0
components.note: 219 MB on disk, 56.2 MB compressed. Only the built frontend and the bundled server are copied in. SIGTERM is handled, so docker stop exits in about 0.2 s with code 0.

components.name: CVE scanners
components.note: Two independent databases. 1.0.0 on node:24-slim showed 7 critical and 15 high in ECR; 1.1.0 on distroless shows none in either scanner.

components.name: Docker Hub
components.note: The public pull source. Anonymous access was checked against the registry API.

components.name: Azure Container Registry
components.tech: Basic · Entra ID · admin user off
components.note: Released and verified, then torn down with its resource group.

components.name: Amazon ECR
components.note: Released and verified, then deleted along with the bootstrap access key.
